Functional and performance tests are generally called unit tests, where a unit refers roughly to a component or the smallest module. Unit tests mainly check that related components interact as expected. From a design perspective, they are written during development to capture your expectations.
Users interact with the interface backed by your source code. Such interactions generally combine an entire subsystem to achieve the expected behavior. These are difficult to cover with unit tests; specialized tests for them are called UI tests.

During a test run, XCTest finds all classes inheriting from XCTestCase and runs their test methods.
For each class, it first runs the class setup method. It creates a fresh instance for each test method and runs that instance's setup method. After the test method, it runs the instance teardown method. This repeats for every method. After the final instance teardown, Xcode runs the class teardown method and proceeds to the next class. The sequence continues until every method in every test class has run.

Product > Perform Action > Test Again: When a test exposes a problem during debugging or editing, returning to the last test is useful.
